RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 5 p.m. 2-5-33 the assistant manager of the
Shanse Theatre, named Kyi Koo Tseu (季周) came to the
Station with the two attached letters and reported that
the same had been received by post on the 2-5-33.

The translation of the letters reads as follows:-

30th April 1933.

Dear Manager,
Shanse Theatre.

We do not know whether you have received a
similar copy of this letter or not.

Now you are showing the film called "City
Morning" produced by the United Photo Play Service in
your theatre and the theatre is very crowded both upstairs
and downstairs. Your business must be prosperous as no
people are admitted into the theatre without tickets.

Our troops have been defeated in the Sino-
Japanese war owing to our lack of aeroplanes.

You are one of the citizens of our country, so
please deduct twenty per cent of your takings from the
"City Morning" and forward same to the Aviation Association
for the relief of the National Salvation Army in the North
East, you should advertise in Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao that
you have acknowledged our request, otherwise we will treat
you with our proper procedure. This is the 2nd letter.
Warning.

LETTER RECEIVED BY GREYHOUND BALL-ROOM MAKING DEMANDS.

At 6.45 p.m. 25-1-33, Mr. Woo, Manager of the Greyhound Ball-Room (Sun Sun Co.), brought a letter to the Station which he stated was received by post at 8.30 a.m. 25-1-33.

A translation of this letter which is given below corresponds with that published in the Intelligence Report of 24-1-33 (Political):-

Management of various local theatres and cinemas:
Though the North East has been lost for over a year, the Government is still in a dilemma. Fortunately, Generals Soo Ping-yen and Vung Chuen-hai put up a desperate resistance against the Japanese and are still continuing their efforts in the field against the enemy. Reading yesterday's newspaper, we learned that some 400 soldiers under the control of General Dung Tien-mei were frozen to death on the "Dah Ku" Mountain, while the people are enjoying their life in the amusement resorts. Such a state of affairs is to be condemned.
